beats.headline: Did you see our signs?
beats.text: For the record: Brandon An, crawler #12,330,671, level six, human, one bronze star, a heavy winter jacket in the heat and a gigantic hammer. Night staff at an eldercare facility in Wenatchee. A fire alarm put all 250 residents out into the freezing street, and the entrance opened in the middle of them. Thirty-eight are here. The plan, such as it is: get them to the second level, then the third, so they can choose a class. "I just can't leave them."

beats.headline: Brandon names it the Speedbump
beats.text: The redoubt was Crawler Carl's idea, but the Andrews brothers are the maintenance men, there that night on overtime to fix an oven, and they know tools. Brandon calls the finished fort The Speedbump. He places wall sections, braces the roof beside Carl, and in the fight swings a giant maul that glitters with lightning. The last tuskling, a level-eight Dominatrix, falls under his hammer. He skips level seven altogether and comes out of it level eight, and shell-shocked.

beats.headline: Twenty-four stayed to sing
beats.text: Only six more residents come down from the Waffle House safe room. Twenty-four voted to stay, and they were all singing when he last saw them. Brandon asks Crawler Carl for help sending the rest down to the third floor early. His boss box gives him a magic boomerang, and a silver star now sits by his name, as by everyone's. When the dungeon announces the rage elemental rule, his first thought is practical: Yolanda had better tell Jack not to pee in the hallways any more.

beats.headline: Wait until you see what we built
beats.text: The people train: ten cars of residents, two by two on their own chairs, linked on one glowing chain. The chain was Imani's idea; Brandon designed the rest and added ramps so they can get on and off. He, Yolanda and his brother went out and cleared the Mind Horrors, a boss that turned out to be a giant blimp, which earned him another bronze star. To Crawler Carl, at the rendezvous: "You are helping us to your own detriment. You are a good man."

beats.headline: A hug at the hole
beats.text: Forty minutes after the elemental dies, what is left of Meadow Lark arrives: thirty-six residents in three shopping-cart contraptions built from chopper wheels. Brandon, weaker than the other two, pushes six people by himself. "We didn't need your directions," he says; the scorched hallway leads straight to the hole. He asks once whether Crawler Carl wants to come with them. Carl does not. Brandon pulls him into a hug. "You two take care of yourselves, okay?"

beats.headline: Selection is slow going
beats.text: A long message, waiting when Crawler Carl wakes. Selection is slow going. No resident can choose human without staying as they are, and the ones with cognitive issues have to pick some really weird races to stay viable. Brandon stayed human. Chris and Imani did not. Most of the residents are still level one and getting Legendary Pacifist Boxes for arriving without killing anything. "I hope we see each other again." Carl replies: find whoever has the manager benefit and talk them into taking it.

beats.headline: Messages from deceased crawlers
beats.text: Filed under Messages from deceased Crawlers. The third floor was about to collapse, and Brandon and a resident named Henry held the line against the shade gremlins so Imani, Elle and the others could reach the stairwell, twenty minutes away with ten on the clock. He had fought with his brother, who left the party and stopped accepting his messages. The message asks Crawler Carl to tell Chris he was sorry, that Chris was right, and that he loved him. "That's the most important part."

beats.headline: The race he made her pick
beats.text: Elle, a Frost Maiden now and floating at the Desperado Club bar, supplies a footnote. She had a long list of races that would have put all her marbles back in the bag. Brandon made her pick the Frost Maiden, a tricky race, because it carries the manager benefit, which Crawler Carl had told him about. Her game guide cried when she chose it. Elle's summary: Brandon was a good kid. Imani's: he died, along with Henry, protecting their escape.

beats.headline: His brother says his name
beats.text: Crawler Carl kept Brandon's last message in his scratch pad and reread it often. He delivered it on the fifth floor, a hand on the shoulder of a petrified man who could not answer: his brother loved him and regretted not saying so, and Brandon gave his life protecting his friends. When the worm is finally out of Chris's head, Chris sits in a daze and says only one thing. "Brandon. Brandon." Carl tells him his brother died saving the lives of a lot of people.
